newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov's FY '98 budget holds spending level.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov's FY '98 budget holds spending level.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland proposed Thursday a $10.16 billion budget for fiscal year 1998 that would hold spending level.
"As I promised in January, the $10.16 billion budget I present to you today holds the line on spending," he said in his budget speech.
The Republican governor also sought an additional $100 million over the next two years for urban economic development projects. Half of that amount was earmarked for Bridgeport.

Rowland called for income tax cuts which would mean $365 million in new tax relief. He said that when combined with cuts of $200 million during his first two years in office, total income tax reductions exceeded $500 million.
The two-year budget provided nearly $2 billion annually in direct aid to municipalities, said Rowland.
He also called for cutting the gasoline tax by five cents per gallon, starting on July 1.
"It is a significant cut that will be visible and have an immediate effect on prices at the pump," he said.
